description: Single-panel CALPHAD line plot (no micrographs) comparing calculated austenite fraction versus temperature for an 8Mn-0.2C (wt.%) alloy at two Al levels and with three thermodynamic databases. The x-axis is T (°C), spanning 600-1400 in 100 °C ticks; the y-axis is Fraction FCC, linear 0-1.0 in 0.1 ticks; no numeric data labels are printed on any curve. The legend encodes Al content by line weight (bold = 6 wt.-% Al, thin = 8 wt.-% Al) and database by style/colour (grey solid = PrecHiMn-01, dash-double-dot = PrecHiMn-02, thin solid black = PrecHiMn-03), giving six curves in total. All six rise to one broad maximum and decay to zero between ~1350 and 1400 °C. PrecHiMn-02 gives the highest fractions: the bold (6 wt.-% Al) curve peaks just below the 0.75 gridline near 950-1000 °C and the thin (8 wt.-% Al) curve near the 0.47 gridline. PrecHiMn-01 gives broader, flatter curves with maxima near 0.43 and 0.41 at ~1050-1100 °C, the thin one starting from zero with an abrupt step at ~650 °C. PrecHiMn-03 gives the lowest fractions, both curves peaking below 0.27, with the thin one stepped at ~750 °C. The figure therefore quantifies how strongly the database choice shifts the predicted austenite stability window during annealing.

observations.observation: The figure is a single line plot of Fraction FCC versus T (°C); it contains no micrographs, maps or tables.
The y-axis is labelled 'Fraction FCC' with a linear scale from 0 to 1.0 in 0.1 increments; the x-axis is labelled 'T ( °C )' from 600 to 1400 in 100 °C increments.

The legend uses line weight to encode Al content (bold = 6 wt.-% Al, thin = 8 wt.-% Al) and line style/colour to encode the database (grey solid = PrecHiMn-01, dash-double-dot = PrecHiMn-02, thin solid black = PrecHiMn-03), yielding six curves.
The highest curve is the bold 6 wt.-% Al PrecHiMn-02 curve, whose maximum lies just below the 0.75 gridline at roughly 950-1000 °C.
The thin 8 wt.-% Al PrecHiMn-02 curve peaks near the 0.47 gridline, well below the bold curve of the same database.
PrecHiMn-01 curves are flatter and broader, with maxima near the 0.43 and 0.41 gridlines at about 1050-1100 °C.
PrecHiMn-03 gives the lowest austenite fractions of the three databases, with both curves peaking below the 0.3 gridline and declining to zero by ~1350 °C.
The 8 wt.-% Al curves computed with PrecHiMn-01 and PrecHiMn-03 are zero below approximately 650 °C and 750 °C respectively, then rise abruptly (step-like) before their gradual decay.
All six curves converge to Fraction FCC = 0 between roughly 1350 and 1400 °C.
The caption states the alloy is 8Mn-0.2C (wt.%) with 6 wt.% and 8 wt.% Al, calculated with three different databases.
The citing text asserts that similar results are observed between the first and the third database version but shifted in temperature.

In the pixels, the PrecHiMn-01 and PrecHiMn-03 curves for the same Al content differ substantially in peak height and peak temperature, not merely by a temperature shift, which does not fully support the citing statement that the two versions give similar results.
The citing text notes there is no agreement between the databases on the three-phase fcc + bcc + j domain that is of primary importance during continuous annealing.
No numeric data-point labels or tabulated values are printed; curve extrema can only be located relative to the 0.1 gridlines.
